trigger: the crash and hang totals were floored on the union cohort (affected_devices) rather than on the devices that contributed each type: 9 devices hang once and 1 device crashes 3 times gives affected_devices 10, crashes 3 and hangs 9, so crashes 3 implies at most 3 crashing devices
classification_rationale: the stats contract says the floor applies to the devices that contributed the events passed alongside it; a union cohort does not satisfy that for a per-type total
summary: Verified on real Postgres with the real join (1.26M-row scale probe): 12 exposed devices, 9 hang once, 1 crashes 3 times, published below_floor false. Extension: only one exposed device crashed 5 times, ten unexposed devices hung once, every existing floor passed and the exposed numerator came from one device.

trigger: at the default observation retention of 30 days the failure window was 30 days; events older than the retention are reaped but the exposure rows live 31 days, so the oldest partial UTC day counted toward exposure with no events and the rate read low by up to about 3 percent (about 50 percent at retention 1 to 7 days)
classification_rationale: the owner header and the reference doc said the two cover the same days, which was false when retention equalled the window
summary: Reporter derived HIGH (wrong rate presented as correct, default configuration); native LOW. Also raised as a NICE by happy-path.

trigger: a version shipped 3 days ago is compared with one present for all 30 days, both with at least 10 exposed devices: the exposure unit is a device count (the per-device days are dropped in the exposure aggregate), so the newer version's rate is biased low and its exact interval looks tight
classification_rationale: the stats header names device-days as the exposure unit for the views; the join passes a device count
summary: Documented only: rate is stated as events per exposed device over the window, not per day of use, and day_count is explained as a days-in-trend-window gauge (c6db1caf2, cc254c60b). Replacing the denominator with device-days contradicts the agreed default of rates per reporting device and is left as a follow-up for the maintainer; open pending that decision.

trigger: crash events and exposure rows canonicalise to different version strings (or differ in subject case or text) for the same installs: 12 devices in the exposure rows on 1.0.0.0 and 600 crashes from the same devices stored under 1.0.0.1 show exposure 12, exposed_crashes 0, rate 0.0 on the first row with nothing flagging the mismatch
classification_rationale: a healthy-looking zero is shown for failures recorded under a neighbouring string; whether every platform emits identical version strings is not verified
summary: Mechanism verified; real-platform premise not verified. Documented only: failures join on the exact canonical version and subject, a row with failures and null exposure is called out, and absence of a row is not absence of failures (9c57827ee, c6db1caf2). Flagging mismatched rows in code remains a maintainer decision; open pending that decision.

trigger: exposed_crashes, exposed_hangs, failure_rate and failure_rate_ratio are floored on the exposure cohort (at least 10 devices), not on the exposed devices that failed, so they can be built from events of 1 to 9 devices; in the wholly-exposed case a withheld total is recoverable verbatim from them
classification_rationale: the headline floor wording understated this exception until the accepted-residual sentences were added
summary: In-force ruling: compliant because the rate's cohort is the exposure population; the band is HIGH only if the maintainer vetoes that ruling. Stated identically in the code banner, the reference doc, the manual, both transport descriptions and the changelog. Listed for the maintainer at the push gate.

trigger: exposure_devices and affected_devices are both published at any size, so with all totals shown their difference (sampled devices with no crash or hang) can be 1 to 9
classification_rationale: the stats contract says to floor complements; the complement carries no events, only the existence of healthy sampled devices
summary: Raised by an external review pass whose report is not committed (reporter_ref unresolved). Ruled as the count-only class the routed row already permits (suppressed points publish device_count); withholding it would hide nearly every healthy version at pilot scale. Listed for the maintainer.

trigger: a caller polls the floored read repeatedly across a rolling window and differences the published figures (also the unfloored per-app totals on the sibling apps read minus floor-passing version rows)
classification_rationale: same class as every rolling-window floored read; no offset or paging parameter exists and the version filter returns the same figures
summary: Derived HIGH only if cross-poll differencing is in scope; recorded as out of scope by the maintainer's decision. One accepted-residual sentence is recommended for the routed row and docs either way. Listed for the maintainer.

trigger: the audit-exemption sentence says the app-performance reads carry only device-state and app-aggregate telemetry; the fleet read now also carries per-app crash and hang counts and exposed rates, and the routed Guardian/DEX clause promising no singling-out is true for points and totals but not for the exposed figures
classification_rationale: persisted policy text that this change makes untrue; neither the first-customer document nor the routed row is edited by the branch
summary: Reviewer supplied exact replacement wording for both the exemption sentence and the routed row clause; the wording and the accepted-residual attribution are the maintainer's to decide, so the files are untouched here. Carried unchanged through round 2.

trigger: an agent syncing about 20 implausibly high version strings (the apply path takes up to 5000 rows) evicts real versions from the default newest-first versions list for up to 180 days; the cap sorts on an agent-controlled key
classification_rationale: degraded completeness of the default view with the version filter still reaching every version and versions_truncated reporting true
summary: Documented in the reference doc (a device reporting implausible versions can push real ones out of the default list; use the version filter). Reviewer rates MEDIUM only if the default view is itself the deliverable. Listed for the maintainer; no code change.

trigger: a fleet of about 30,000 agents: the read takes 1 to 2.5 seconds because no index leads with the application; pilot scale measures 98 to 180 ms hot
classification_rationale: an index change is governed by the Postgres store contract and its own review, not by this change
summary: Evidence (EXPLAIN with buffers, latency) is to be recorded in the pull request body; no index added here.

trigger: the new read degrades (pool acquire timeout, statement error, store not open) and only a log line records it; sibling reads expose a degrade counter by reason
classification_rationale: observability for a new read path; the log now carries the SQLSTATE but there is no counter
summary: A reason-labelled degrade counter (application name must not be a label) was recommended and not added; the SQLSTATE log line was added in 9c57827ee.

trigger: sixteen concurrent loads of the read each take a lease from the shared pool and saturate it for about 0.5 to 1.3 seconds; under a table lock ten of ten other-store bounded acquires failed and one blocked read held 10.03 seconds
classification_rationale: bounded acquire (3 s) and statement timeout (10 s) hold, so this is contention rather than a wedge; sustained starvation is the only band-raising case
summary: Optional route-level concurrency cap (existing read-cap precedent) or documentation not added; the 503 degrade and recovery after release were verified.

trigger: a degraded read advertises a retry hint of 2000 ms although the statement budget is 10 seconds
classification_rationale: the hint is optimistic against the statement budget; callers still get a typed 503 and retry
summary: Shared across REST and the MCP twin through one constant; left unchanged.

trigger: the operator raises the observation retention (for example 7 to 30 days) and restarts: rows keep the expiry stamped at ingest under the old value, but the owner now takes the new value and reads the longer window, so for up to the window length events cover fewer days than the exposure rows and the rate reads low with nothing flagging it
classification_rationale: the reference text claimed no counted day has had its events reaped, which is false during that transient
summary: Derived HIGH (non-default configuration change plus a transient); native LOW. Reviewer recommended one accepted-residual sentence and no code change.

trigger: an owner row that violates the SQL invariants (negative device count, exposed devices above total devices, zero devices with a non-zero total) is published as not withheld
classification_rationale: the counts come from a distinct count over a non-null column with a filtered subset, so the shape cannot be produced today; only a future owner change or a test double could reach it
summary: Independently noted by cpp-safety at the same site (no overflow, sanitiser clean). Optional hardening: treat a negative devices or remainder value as withheld. Not applied.

Fixed in 9c57827ee: four per-type distinct-device columns in the owner SQL; each total (crashes, hangs) is withheld when its own devices number 1 to 9 or, with the exposed figures shown, when its devices outside the exposure cohort do; below_floor is true when either is withheld. Round 2 re-ran the shapes on real Postgres and a 6000-case spec sweep (0 mismatches); mutants of the floor, remainder and union-cohort forms all went red. The exposed-numerator residual is recorded separately.

Fixed in 9c57827ee: the window is clamped to one day less than the retention when that is positive (30 and 31 or more give 29 and 30; unbounded keeps 30), with pure clamp and SQL boundary tests; round 2 re-derived that no counted day has lost events. A retention raise followed by a restart is the separate transient recorded as the retention-raise finding.

Resolved in cc254c60b by one accepted-residual sentence in the failure window bullet of the REST reference (raising retention and restarting widens the window at once but does not restore reaped events, so counts and rate can read low for up to the window length; lowering is safe). No code change, as recommended; the derived HIGH stands as a documented accepted residual rather than a closed defect.

There is no floor for the exposed figures to be built around, so the finding's premise no longer applies.
